title: A proper birational morphism to a normal integral curve is an isomorphism
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $C$ and $E$ be integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] separated schemes of finite type over $k$, each of dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; thus both are curves over $k$ in the sense of [def-pc-curve]. Let $p:E\to C$ be a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] dominant $k$-morphism inducing an isomorphism of function fields $k(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}k(E)$. If every local ring of $C$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], then $p$ is an isomorphism. No normality of $E$ and no perfection assumption on $k$ are required.

source.place: Tag 0AB7 (lemma-finite-in-codim-1) gives finiteness for a proper birational map of integral curves; Tag 0BFP (lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1) gives the isomorphism over the normal curve. Equivalently finish with morphisms.tex Tag 0AB1 (lemma-finite-birational-over-normal).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-proper-birational-curve-finite] to the given proper dominant morphism. Its hypotheses hold because $C$ and $E$ are integral separated finite-type $k$-schemes of dimension $1$, and the stated function-field isomorphism is exactly the birational hypothesis. The proof of Tag 0AB7 applies its codimension-one finiteness criterion at every point of the one-dimensional Noetherian target $C$; finiteness is local on the target, so $p$ is finite.

Now [lem-trf-finite-birational-normal-iso] applies to $p$: the finiteness is Step 1, the function-field isomorphism is part of the item hypothesis, and the assumption that every local ring of $C$ is an integrally closed domain is precisely normality of the target in that node. It follows that $p$ is an isomorphism. The argument uses no normality of $E$ and no perfection assumption on $k$.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0AB7 and 0BFP, with the equivalent final application of Tag 0AB1 in morphisms.tex.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q17-a4764da6d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, both new nodes and every cited definition. Sources checked: Stacks Tag 0AB7 (varieties.tex l.3268, lemma-finite-in-codim-1), Tag 0BFP (l.3300) and Tag 0AB1 (morphisms.tex l.14630, lemma-finite-birational-over-normal). Step 1 applies lem-trf-proper-birational-curve-finite, which is true by 0AB7 condition (1): C has Noetherian local rings of dimension at most 1, dominance sends the generic point of E to the generic point of C, the function-field extension is an isomorphism, and finiteness is local on the target. Step 2 applies lem-trf-finite-birational-normal-iso, which is true by 0AB1: on affine opens the ring inclusion keeps the fraction field, the cover is integral and the target ring is integrally closed. Every hypothesis matches the item; neither step uses normality of E or a perfect field. Small cases: identity of A^1; the open immersion of A^1 minus a point (not proper, not finite); the normalization of a cusp (shows the normality hypothesis is needed); blow-up of A^2 (dimension 2, excluded). Duplicate candidates read and judged different: pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite, lem-sbc-finite-normal-dense-open-iso, lem-sbc-normalization-dense-open, lem-sbc-normal-dense-open-integral-section, lem-sc-normalization-properties. Neither new node restates a clause of the item, and there is no cycle. All three nodes stay in unit sk-i-curve-zero, so there are no tool_uses. No SGA source is used. The item statement is unchanged from base.
